---
title: "Versioned sites"
---


A published link should keep meaning what it meant when somebody set
it. The deployment layout the zotQDA sites use — and that this theme
supports with two small pieces — makes that a property of the file
system, not a promise:

```
example.org/
├── index.html      ← bare-address shortcut, forwards to latest/
├── versions.json   ← the list the version switcher reads
├── 0.1.0/          ← one directory per release, never touched again
├── 0.2.0/
└── latest/         ← a second copy of the newest release
```

Every release is uploaded into its own directory and never modified
afterwards; `latest/` follows the newest release only. Rebuilding the
documentation of an older release refreshes its own directory and
leaves `latest/` alone.

## versions.json and gen_versions.py

`versions.json` sits at the site root, one directory above the version
directories. `script/gen_versions.py` maintains it from the one place
the version already lives — `manifest.json`, `src/*/_version.py`, a
`DESCRIPTION` file or an `_extensions/*/_extension.yml`, whichever the
repository has:

```sh
python script/gen_versions.py            # add the current version
python script/gen_versions.py --current  # just print it (the deploy asks here)
```

Adding a version is a change to a committed file, deliberately: a
release that quietly appeared in the switcher and nowhere else would
be hard to account for later.

## The version banner

`shared/versions.js` — inlined into every page by
[gen_langmap.py](multilingual.qmd) — adds the three things that make
the layout usable: a note saying which version you are reading, a menu
to reach the same page in another version, and a warning when the
version is not the current release. Legal pages are retargeted to the
newest version, so an outdated Impressum can never be the one a
visitor lands on.

Everything is conditional on the address actually carrying a version
segment. In help bundled into a plugin, or in a plain file tree, the
banner does nothing at all — which is correct: that copy belongs to
the release it shipped with.

## The deploy that fits this layout

`examples/site-publish.yml` sketches the workflow; the qdaPy and qdaR
repositories carry the full version in production (`docs.yml`: build,
smoketest, then an SFTP mirror **into the version directory only**,
with the host key pinned and a guard that refuses to operate on an
account root). This site deploys the same way.
